title: ECharts in RO style
text: Load packages need: use small synthetic dataset throughout vignette can run everything standalone:
code: library(echarts4r) library(dplyr) # library(ROvis) library(ROvis.echarts) library(ROvis.utils) sex_levels <- c("Women", "Men", "Total")  # Reported cases per age group and sex dat_cases <- data.frame(   agegroup = rep(c("0-19", "20-39", "40-59", "60-79", "80+"), times = 3),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 5), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     12000,     48000,     61000,     43000,     18000,     10000,     45000,     58000,     39000,     14000,     22000,     93000,     119000,     82000,     32000   ) )  # Reported cases per week (three series) dat_weekly <- data.frame(   week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 12), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     800,     950,     1100,     1400,     1600,     1550,     1300,     1100,     900,     750,     600,     500,     700,     880,     1020,     1300,     1480,     1420,     1180,     990,     820,     680,     540,     440,     1500,     1830,     2120,     2700,     3080,     2970,     2480,     2090,     1720,     1430,     1140,     940   ) )

title: ECharts in RO style
text: ro_e_theme() applies RO visual style echarts4r chart. slots echarts4r pipeline way ro_gg_theme() ggplot2. Add end, chart layers:
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: grouped charts, group data dplyr::group_by() piping e_charts():
code: dat_cases |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n) |>   e_title("Cases by age group and sex") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme(palette = "gender_con")

title: ECharts in RO style
text: Use e_flip_coords() turn column chart horizontal bar chart:
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_flip_coords() |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: note x-axis variable types: x-axis variable numeric (like year week number), echarts4r treats value axis. RO theme shows grid lines value axes, end vertical grid lines well horizontal ones. avoid , make x-axis variable factor explicit levels. way echarts4r uses category axis, grid lines, order values stays correct. example, achieved : convenience, also warning displayed try :
code: dat_weekly |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_title("Weekly cases by sex") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme(palette = "gender_con") # Turns week into a category axis without changing the order week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12) data_multi <- data.frame(   year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024),   women = c(120, 145, 160, 175, 190),   men = c(95, 110, 125, 140, 150) )  data_multi |>   e_charts(year) |>   e_bar(women, name = "Women") |>   e_bar(men, name = "Men") |>   ro_e_theme(palette = "gender_con") ## Warning: ! The x-axis variable is numeric, which creates a continuous axis. ## ℹ If not intended, convert the variable to a factor: `mutate(year = ##   factor(year))`

title: ECharts in RO style
code: tab_cases_week_by_prov <- expand.grid(   week = seq(as.Date("2022-04-01"), by = "week", length.out = 20),   Province = c("Flevoland", "Groningen", "Noord-Brabant", "Utrecht", "Zeeland") ) |>   mutate(n = sample(10:1000, n(), replace = TRUE))  tab_cases_week_by_prov |>   group_by(Province) |>   e_charts(x = week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases") |>   e_x_axis(     name = "Date",     formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(       'function (value) {     var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",                            "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];     var d = new Date(value);     return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();   }'     )   ) |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_title("Cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>   e_legend() |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>   ro_e_theme()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: default, ro_e_theme() enforces fixed aspect ratios accordance RO data visualisation guidelines: total element (title + chart + legend) 2:1 width--height, inner plot area (grid , without axis labels legend) 3:1 width--height. ratios update automatically whenever container width changes, example browser window resized Shiny sidebar toggled. controlled fixed_aspect argument, defaults TRUE. Set fixed_aspect = FALSE need control chart height , example inside Shiny app fixed-height container dashboard chart must fill exact pixel area. chart keeps height specify (via e_charts(height = …) chunk’s fig.height option) stops adjusting resize:
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("2:1 aspect ratio (default)", "fixed_aspect = TRUE") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme() dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup, height = 400) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("Fixed 400 px height (fixed_aspect = FALSE)") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme(fixed_aspect = FALSE)

title: ECharts in RO style
text: ro_e_theme() accepts palette argument. available palettes ones used ro_color_palette(): "categorical" (default) general categorical data "gender_con" conventional gender colors "gender_unc" unconventional gender colors "full" 18 RO colors "greys" grey tints can preview palette ro_show_colors(): Apply different palette passing name ro_e_theme():
code: ro_show_colors("categorical") ro_show_colors("gender_con") ro_show_colors("gender_unc") ro_show_colors("greys") dat_cases |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n) |>   e_title("Cases by age group and sex", "gender_unc palette") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme(palette = "gender_unc")

title: ECharts in RO style
text: Interactive charts need accessible keyboard-users. ro_e_keyboard_nav() adds keyboard controls top ro_e_theme(): Arrow keys move tooltip across data points. direction auto-detected chart orientation (left/right column line charts, /horizontal bar charts). can also set explicitly axis. Letter keys toggle individual series . Use series_keys argument map single letter series name. Add ro_e_keyboard_nav() last step pipeline: assign “w” “Women”, “m” “Men”, “t” “Total”. can also extent . example, case Dutch provinces: Note names must single letters values must exactly match series names chart. horizontal bar chart, ro_e_keyboard_nav() auto-detects vertical orientation binds /arrow keys instead:
code: dat_weekly |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_title(     "Weekly cases by sex",     "Use arrow keys to navigate, W/M to toggle series"   ) |>   e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme(palette = "gender_con") |>   ro_e_keyboard_nav(series_keys = c(w = "Women", m = "Men", t = "Total")) tab_cases_week_by_prov |>   group_by(Province) |>   e_charts(x = week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases", x = "Date") |>   e_x_axis(     formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(       'function (value) {     var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",                            "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];     var d = new Date(value);     return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();   }'     )   ) |>   e_title("COVID-19 cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>   e_legend() |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>   ro_e_theme() |>   ro_e_keyboard_nav(     series_keys = c(       f = "Flevoland",       g = "Groningen",       n = "Noord-Brabant",       u = "Utrecht",       z = "Zeeland"     ),     axis = "both"   ) dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_flip_coords() |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Use up/down arrow keys to navigate") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme() |>   ro_e_keyboard_nav()

title: Apply the RO echarts theme to an echarts4r object — ro_e_theme
text: e echarts4r object (created echarts4r::e_charts()). palette Character. Palette use series colors. One "categorical" (default), "gender_con", "gender_unc". Passed ro_color_palette(). fixed_aspect Logical. TRUE (default), total element (title + chart + legend) maintains 2:1 width--height ratio, inner plot area (grid , excluding axis labels legend) maintains 3:1 width--height ratio. ratios update responsively resize. Set FALSE let chart fill whatever height container provides (useful embedding fixed-size layout Shiny app explicit height). font NULL (default) character string naming system font family. NULL, RijksoverheidSansWebText used installed, otherwise Verdana. Supply font name override chart labels custom HTML legend. warning issued font found system. renderer renderer use. One "svg" "canvas". Defaults "svg" comply accessibility standards.
